subject: Renewal uplift — phased incentive plan and co-term request
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Draft: phased incentive + co-term option for Arbor renewal (need inputs)

Team —

I pulled together an initial approach for Arbor Retail's upcoming renewal (renewal window: Aug 1). They signaled they want a smoother ramp for expanded committed capacity and asked for a co-term to simplify procurement. High-level idea below — looking for feedback on concession sizing and billing timing before I send to Kyle next week.

Summary proposal (initial):
- Renewal uplift: convert to a staged uplift over 12 months (vs. single-step) — target uplift ~15–20% of current committed tokens over year 1.
- Incentive credits: front-load a small onboarding credit (5% equivalent) to offset first-quarter churn risk.
- Co-term: offer option to co-term to Jan 31, 2028 (aligns with enterprise billing), with an annual true-up at co-term date.
- Flexibility: include a one-time capacity burst window for holiday season (72-hr notice, subject to quota).
- Pricing guardrails: tiered unit price that steps down as committed volume hits thresholds (to protect Redwood unit economics).

Open questions for finance/legal:
1) Is 5% onboarding credit acceptable from a margin perspective?
2) If customer asks to annualize earlier (6 months), can we prorate the onboarding credit?
3) Do we want to include a firm SLA uplift (latency) for the dedicated portion, or offer SLA as optional add-on?

Please review the attached concession_matrix.xlsx — I added three concession scenarios (conservative / baseline / aggressive) and a quick P&L view. Specific asks: Monica — please sanity-check the margin assumptions. Lauren — can you confirm co-term language and procurement timing? Aditya — flag any billing / invoice timing constraints.

If we agree, I’ll draft a one-pager to send to Kyle with two clear choices (baseline + expedited co-term) and ask for a decision by June 9.

Thanks,
Sean
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment: concession_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft: phased incentive + co-term option for Arbor renewal (need inputs)

Sean —

Nice framework. Quick thoughts after running the conservative/baseline/aggressive sheets:
- 5% onboarding credit is fine under baseline, but drop to 3% in conservative scenario (keeps EBITDA impact < 2.2% on year 1).
- For the tiered unit price, recommend making thresholds explicit (e.g., 0–500M tokens, 500–1B, 1B+) and lock the step discounts for the 12-month term only.
- Co-term to Jan 31, 2028 is workable, but procurement at Arbor sometimes needs an extra 30 days — suggest we surface a fallback co-term date 28-Feb-2028 in the offer language. That gives them a clear path and reduces back-and-forth.
- On SLA: I prefer offering a paid SLA add-on. If they insist, we can provide a 99.9% uptime commitment for the dedicated pool at a 7.5% price premium.

I updated concession_matrix.xlsx with a 3/4/5% credit tier for conservative/baseline/aggressive. Also added a payment cadence alternative (Net30 vs Net45) — see sheet 'billing_options'.

If you want, I can draft the legal-friendly paragraph for co-term + true-up (short, plain English) for you to send to Kyle.

-Monica
Monica Patel
Lead Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 6 Jun 2027 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: Renewal + phased uplift incentive (two options)

Kyle —

Thanks again for the candid conversation last week. As promised, attached is a concise proposal with two straightforward options: 1) Baseline renewal with phased uplift and 3% onboarding credit, or 2) Accelerated renewal with larger volume discounts if you commit to a 12-month increased capacity profile. Both include an optional co-term to Jan 31, 2028 (we listed Feb 28, 2028 as a fallback if your procurement needs the additional window).

Key points (Baseline offer):
- Year 1 uplift: phased +15% over current committed tokens, applied monthly to smooth cost impact.
- Onboarding credit: 3% credit applied to first invoice after renewal activation.
- Billing: Net30 preferred; Net45 available as a deferred option under the accelerated offer.
- Co-term: optional to Jan 31, 2028 (fallback Feb 28, 2028). Annual true-up at co-term date.
- Capacity burst: one 72-hr burst window (subject to 72-hr notice).

Accelerated offer includes steeper volume break points and 5% onboarding credit upfront. I attached the one-page summary and the full proposal PDF for procurement.

Next steps: If either option looks good, can you confirm preferred co-term date and billing cadence? Once we have that, I’ll route the final SOW to legal for a lightweight amendment so procurement can start a PO.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20-min call if that helps.

Best,
Sean

Attachment: Arbor_renewal_proposal.pdf
From: Kyle Morris <kyle.morris@arborretail.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@arborretail.com
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: Renewal + phased uplift incentive (two options)

Sean —

Appreciate the clear options and the one-pager. Internal procurement forwarded the PDF to our legal team and they had a couple of asks:

1) Can we tighten the uplift in year 1 to +10% instead of +15% for the baseline? We’re comfortable with the accelerated option if the 5% onboarding credit is included, but procurement wants a lower baseline number to start.
2) Co-term: we’d prefer co-term to Feb 28, 2028 (procurement needs the extra month).
3) Billing: procurement asks for Net45 on the first two invoices during the ramp period, then Net30 afterwards.

I attached our PO_template.pdf — if you can provide a one-page amendment that reflects: (a) +10% baseline uplift, (b) Feb 28, 2028 co-term, (c) Net45 first two invoices, we can route a signed LOI and get the procurement team to issue a PO.

Can you confirm margin impact on your side? If you can accept the baseline at +10% with the 3% onboarding credit and the Net45 ramp cadence, I’ll get the LOI to you by next Tue. Otherwise happy to discuss the accelerated option.

Thanks,
Kyle Morris
Head of Platform Partnerships, Arbor Retail
kyle.morris@arborretail.com
